cohort: 96 first-time mothers who gave birth via vaginal delivery (n=38), emergency C-section (n=27), or planned C-section (n=21)
finding: Early postpartum depressive symptoms predicted later PTSD symptoms in first-time mothers, suggesting that early detection and intervention for postpartum depression might also prevent PTSD development.
mod_finding: While the study stratified by mode of delivery, no moderating effect of mode of delivery was found on the relationship between postpartum depression and PTSD symptoms.
